newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UK's Cadbury opens Russian chocolate plant.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cadbury opens Russian chocolate plant.

text.p: UK confectioner Cadbury Schweppes Plc officially opened a chocolate plant on Friday near Russia's northwestern city of St Petersburg, its biggest greenfield project outside Britain,
A Cadbury statement said the 40,000-tonne-a-year facility produced its first chocolate last October but that the official opening was held over until Friday.
The plant is situated in the town of Chudovo to the north of the Novgorod region and employs 280 people.

"This is a significant investment for Cadbury Schweppes and confirms our commitment to the Russian market and our intention to build a successful long term business," Sir Dominic Cadbury, chairman of Cadbury Schweppes, said in the statement.

Western confectionery giants have been marketing their products hard in Russia since economic reforms began in 1991, but the latest development in the battle for market share involves foreign firms setting up operations on Russian soil.

The Chudovo factory will supply the Russian market and export confectionery to other Commonwealth of Independent States countries. The plant produces brands including Cadbury's Picnic, Wispa, Dairy Milk and Fruit & Nut.
